projects.title: Byte Lab
projects.contract: byte-lab 0..4294967295 → dec=N hex=XXXXXXXX bits=32-bit-string ones=N
projects.steps: Parse with strtoull; reject signs, whitespace, suffixes and range errors. Convert using shifts on uint32_t. Count bits without shifting a signed value.
projects.insight: An integer value is abstract; its in-memory byte order is a separate concern. Use PRI macros rather than assuming unsigned long is 32 bits.
projects.solution: An end pointer distinguishes valid zero from conversion failure; fixed-width unsigned arithmetic makes every shift well-defined.
projects.stretch: Add binary input, byte-order inspection through unsigned char, and rotate-left with a zero-shift guard.

projects.title: Hex Detective
projects.contract: hexview < binary-file → offset: hex bytes, 16 bytes per row
projects.steps: Read fread blocks of 16; emit offsets as eight hex digits and bytes as two. Never store EOF in char. Distinguish ferror from EOF.
projects.insight: Text functions lose embedded NUL. Bytes are unsigned; the file may contain any of 256 values.
projects.solution: A fixed stack buffer bounds memory; a partial final block is printed exactly once.
projects.stretch: Add an ASCII sidebar and reverse mode; compare against xxd, then benchmark 1 MiB blocks.

projects.title: Persian UTF-8 Scanner
projects.contract: utf8 < text → bytes=N codepoints=N; malformed UTF-8 exits 2
projects.steps: Classify lead bytes; accumulate continuation bytes; reject overlong sequences, surrogates, values above U+10FFFF and truncated sequences.
projects.insight: strlen counts bytes, not Persian letters. A code point is also not necessarily one visible grapheme.
projects.solution: The decoder enforces shortest encodings and scalar-value validity; it does not normalize, shape, or count graphemes.
projects.stretch: Print each scalar as U+XXXX; later explore combining marks and why grapheme segmentation needs Unicode data.

projects.title: Vector Workshop
projects.contract: vector INT... → sorted integer line; at least one integer
projects.steps: Design a vector with data/len/cap. Grow geometrically with overflow checks. Store realloc in a temporary. Sort with a comparator that cannot overflow.
projects.insight: A successful realloc may invalidate every pointer into the old allocation; len and cap have different meanings.
projects.solution: The reference doubles capacity, keeps a single owning pointer, and compares with relational operators instead of subtraction.
projects.stretch: Expose push/pop/reserve in a header and add allocator injection to exercise allocation failure.

projects.title: Word Frequency Map
projects.contract: wordmap < text → lexically sorted lowercase ASCII word=count lines
projects.steps: Tokenize ASCII letters only. Hash each word into buckets. Compare full keys on collision. Copy owned keys, collect entries, sort and free every allocation.
projects.insight: A matching hash is not a matching key. Explicitly choose ASCII semantics rather than pretending to support Persian words.
projects.solution: Chained buckets trade simplicity for extra allocations; iteration is sorted separately because hash order is unstable.
projects.stretch: Implement resizing and a collision-heavy test; extend tokenization using project 03 without confusing byte and character boundaries.

projects.title: CSV State Machine
projects.contract: csv < input → rows=N fields=N max_fields=N; invalid input exits 2
projects.steps: Track field start, unquoted, quoted and after-quote states. Handle escaped double quotes and embedded newlines. Accept LF record endings, not CRLF. Count empty fields.
projects.insight: A comma is data inside quotes. Splitting with strtok cannot parse CSV and loses empty fields.
projects.solution: Four states make every legal transition visible; EOF is a transition too, especially inside an unfinished quote.
projects.stretch: Add CRLF support and emit structured records; document whether a blank line is an empty record.

projects.title: Tiny Grep
projects.contract: grep PATTERN [-i] < text → 1-based-number:line; 0 matches exits 1
projects.steps: Read getline lines. Search a literal pattern without changing displayed text. Implement ASCII case-insensitivity with unsigned byte comparisons. Return 0/1/2 for match/no-match/error.
projects.insight: User-facing exit status is an API; scripts depend on the difference between empty results and an error.
projects.solution: A simple bounded comparison avoids temporary lowercase copies and preserves original output. This is deliberately literal matching, not regex.
projects.stretch: Add -n, -v and multiple files; implement a separate KMP matcher and measure worst-case input.

projects.title: Arena Allocator
projects.contract: arena SIZE|reset ... → aligned offset or reset; capacity 4096 bytes
projects.steps: Use max_align_t alignment. Round offsets with checked arithmetic; reject zero/oversized requests. Reset invalidates all previous allocations.
projects.insight: Arena memory is freed as a group. It is suitable when object lifetimes end together, not as a general malloc replacement.
projects.solution: A union supplies alignment and storage; offsets are checked before addition, and reset only rewinds the cursor.
projects.stretch: Add marks/rewind and poisoning in debug builds; use an arena for parsing expression nodes.

projects.title: Bookish Reading Ledger
projects.contract: ledger FILE add TEXT | list → added or numbered entries
projects.steps: Treat one UTF-8 string as one record. Reject newline/CR and cap entry length at 4096 bytes. Append, fflush then fsync; list with getline.
projects.insight: A successful printf is not a durability guarantee. Even fsync alone does not create transaction semantics for concurrent writers.
projects.solution: A line format is inspectable and easy to recover manually; this single-writer exercise intentionally has no updates or database locking.
projects.stretch: Add timestamps and atomic export; inject a write error with /dev/full and design a multi-writer lock.

projects.title: Expression Interpreter
projects.contract: calc "EXPR" → numeric result; invalid/non-finite/division-by-zero exits 2
projects.steps: Parse expression → term → unary → primary. Honor parentheses and whitespace. Check finite results and cap recursion at 128. Consume all input.
projects.insight: Operator precedence is grammar structure, not a pile of ad-hoc string splits. Floating point is not exact decimal money arithmetic.
projects.solution: Returning a value plus parser error state keeps control flow simple; a depth limit makes nested hostile input bounded.
projects.stretch: Add variables and ASTs; compare a tree interpreter against project 17 bytecode.

projects.title: Pocket POSIX Shell
projects.contract: shell -c "COMMAND [| COMMAND...]" → child output and last-command status
projects.steps: Parse whitespace-separated argv and |. Create pipes, fork all children before waiting, close unused ends in both processes and collect every child. No quotes, redirection, globbing or job control.
projects.insight: If the parent keeps a write end open, the reader never sees EOF. Waiting before starting a pipeline consumer can deadlock.
projects.solution: Each process inherits descriptors; ownership is made explicit. The last child determines pipeline status while every child is reaped.
projects.stretch: Add quoting with a tokenizer, then redirection, process groups, signals and job control as separate milestones.

projects.title: HTTP Request Inspector
projects.contract: http-parse < CRLF request → method=GET target=/... version=HTTP/1.1 headers=N
projects.steps: Read at most 8192 bytes. Require a single complete header block, exact HTTP/1.1 request line, token header names and visible header values. Require exactly one nonempty Host. Reject bodies, Transfer-Encoding and nonzero Content-Length.
projects.insight: HTTP is framed bytes, not arbitrary lines. Ambiguous framing invites request-smuggling bugs.
projects.solution: The contract only accepts GET requests without bodies, and rejects duplicates of framing headers instead of guessing.
projects.stretch: Add body framing in a separate parser with an explicit byte limit; use a fuzzer on every parser state.

projects.title: Loopback Health Server
projects.contract: http-server PORT → READY=PORT; GET /health returns 200 JSON, unknown path 404
projects.steps: Bind 127.0.0.1; allow port 0 for tests. Read until CRLFCRLF with an 8192-byte limit and timeout. Parse with the same strict HTTP subset as project 12. Send complete responses with Content-Length; handle SIGPIPE.
projects.insight: TCP preserves a byte stream, not your send boundaries. One recv is not one request.
projects.solution: One connection at a time keeps descriptor ownership clear; timeouts bound slow clients. This teaching server is not an Internet-facing production server.
projects.stretch: Use poll with many sockets; measure slow-client behavior before implementing keep-alive.

projects.title: Append-Only KV Store
projects.contract: kvlog FILE put KEY VALUE | get KEY | del KEY; absent get exits 1
projects.steps: Use printable ASCII keys/values without tabs/newlines, max 255/1023 bytes. Append put/del records and fsync. Replay records in order; ignore a trailing torn record and truncate it before the next append.
projects.insight: A log is a history; a map is its current interpretation. Recovery rules are part of the file format.
projects.solution: A deliberately small tab-delimited format demonstrates replay and tail repair. It has no checksum, concurrent writer safety or crash-atomic transaction guarantee.
projects.stretch: Add record length and checksum, atomic compaction with directory fsync, indexing and file locks; study SQLite rather than calling this a SQLite clone.

projects.title: LRU Cache Simulator
projects.contract: lru CAPACITY KEY... → hit=N miss=N cache=most-recent,...
projects.steps: Move a hit to the front; allocate a miss; evict the tail above capacity. Maintain head/tail and prev/next links. Cap capacity at 10000.
projects.insight: A cache is an explicit policy plus lookup; a linked list alone makes lookup O(capacity).
projects.solution: The reference favors a transparent list over an optimized hash/list combination, so you can inspect every invariant.
projects.stretch: Reuse project 05 for O(1)-average lookup; test capacity 1, repeated eviction and failed allocation.

projects.title: Parallel Checksum Lab
projects.contract: workers THREADS COUNT → sum=N for 1..COUNT; threads 1..64, count <= 10000000
projects.steps: Split the integer range into disjoint intervals. Give each thread private job/result storage. Join all started workers before reading and reducing results.
projects.insight: A thread result needs a lifetime that outlasts the thread. Shared mutable counters require synchronization.
projects.solution: Partitioned ownership removes the need for locks; joining establishes the handoff. This is a parallel reduction, not a general thread pool.
projects.stretch: Turn it into a bounded producer/consumer queue with condition variables; test cancellation, shutdown and ThreadSanitizer separately.

projects.title: Stack Bytecode VM
projects.contract: vm < instructions: PUSH N, ADD, SUB, MUL, DIV, PRINT → printed values
projects.steps: Parse one strict instruction per line. Use an int64_t stack of 1024 slots. Check overflow, underflow, zero division and INT64_MIN/-1. Reject unknown opcodes and operands.
projects.insight: A VM must treat bytecode as untrusted input even if its own compiler produced it. Integer overflow in C is undefined behavior.
projects.solution: A small instruction set isolates dispatch and stack semantics; overflow helpers turn undefined arithmetic into predictable errors.
projects.stretch: Compile project 10 ASTs to this VM; add jumps, instruction budgets and a verifier before adding loops.

projects.title: Local Document Index
projects.contract: search CORPUS WORD → matching 1-based document IDs; 0 hits exits 1
projects.steps: One LF-delimited line is one document. Tokenize lowercase ASCII words; map each token to a deduplicated posting list. Search exactly one ASCII word and emit sorted IDs.
projects.insight: A scan and an index can return the same answer with different costs. A word repeated in a document must not duplicate the document ID.
projects.solution: The reference builds an in-memory inverted index with owned word and posting storage; persistence and ranking remain explicit extensions.
projects.stretch: Add AND/OR intersections and BM25; integrate project 03 for Persian-aware tokenization and measure retrieval quality.

projects.title: Python ↔ C Bridge
projects.contract: libcourse.so exports int course_utf8_count(const unsigned char*,size_t,size_t*)
projects.steps: Export one stable function. Validate pointer/length combinations; report scalar count via an out parameter. Compile -fPIC -shared, declare ctypes argtypes/restype and test embedded NUL.
projects.insight: Python memory ownership does not transfer to C just because a pointer crosses the ABI. C must not keep borrowed buffers.
projects.solution: Caller-owned byte buffers and an out parameter avoid ambiguous allocation ownership. size_t must map to ctypes.c_size_t.
projects.stretch: Expose search as a handle API with create/query/destroy; package bindings with ABI version checks.

projects.title: Document Search API
projects.contract: doc-api PORT CORPUS → READY=PORT; GET /health or /search?q=ASCIIword returns JSON
projects.steps: Load a corpus, build an inverted index, serve loopback HTTP with the strict framing from projects 12/13, decode %XX and +, validate one word and return IDs. Define 400/404 and missing-corpus behavior.
projects.insight: A capstone proves interfaces compose. Correct HTTP, ownership and search semantics matter more than adding a frontend.
projects.solution: The reference combines the index and HTTP modules without duplicating protocol parsing. It is sequential, in-memory and ASCII-search only.
projects.stretch: Add Persian tokenization, persistent snapshots, LRU results, a bounded worker queue and a Python client; create benchmarks before claiming performance.
